traits.precision: How exactly a detected box matches a real clickable element (and carries a stable ref).
traits.coverage: How many kinds of screens the detector can read: any pixels versus only a live browser page.
traits.privacy: How little the screenshot travels: on-machine detection scores highest.

evidence: libs/core/ui-element-detector.ts (BrowserDomDetector: boxes are the browser snapshot's getBoundingClientRect of interactive elements with @eN refs; only available when a browser snapshot of the same viewport is supplied)
libs/core/ui-element-detector.ts (OcrTextDetector: text lines from the ocr-provider seam in mode 'local_only' by default; finds labelled controls on any screenshot but not unlabelled icons)

libs/core/os-accessibility-detector.ts (OsAccessibilityDetector: boxes are the OS accessibility tree's position/size of interactive elements in the front window, macOS System Events via JXA, one Apple event per property per tree level (~0.2 s per level measured on macOS 2026-09-27); only available when the request declares live_screen, the platform is darwin and AXIsProcessTrusted passes; native apps on this machine's live screen only, no Windows UI Automation yet)

libs/core/pixel-region-detector.ts (PixelRegionDetector: deterministic on-machine edge/connected-component regions of any screenshot; finds unlabelled icons and buttons OCR misses, but boxes are unlabelled guesses that can include text blocks and decorations)

precision.description: Click targets must be exact; prefer detectors whose boxes are real elements with stable refs.

coverage.description: Any screen (native apps, remote desktops, images): prefer detectors that read pixels, including unlabelled icons.

speed.description: Interactive loops where marking latency matters most.

privacy.description: Prefer the screenshot to stay on this machine.

grounding.description: Default when no browser snapshot is available: exact element sources first (accessibility on a live screen), then labelled text, then raw pixel regions.
